advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass the fold's starting tip as update-ref's expected old-value (CAS) as the plan specified, or document why the write lock makes CAS unnecessary.
evidence: ticket bcfb-0d18-20fc-46b9 plan step 2: 'git update-ref refs/heads/<ref> <merged> <old-tip> — a compare-and-swap, so a concurrent mover aborts the heal instead of clobbering'
tip captured at s3_doctor.py:262 `probe = _git(base_path, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{branch}^{{commit}}")` but not passed as an expected old value to update-ref
advisory.finding: _publish_ref moves refs/heads/<ref> with a plain `update-ref branch merged_sha` and no old-value argument, so it is not the compare-and-swap the ticket plan specified ('git update-ref refs/heads/<ref> <merged> <old-tip> — a compare-and-swap, so a concurrent mover aborts the heal instead of clobbering'). The tip is read at s3_doctor.py:262 and written at s3_doctor.py:322 with nothing guaranteeing the ref still points at the value the fold started from; the write lock only guards other rebar processes on the same tracker, not a concurrent git/tool mutation of the branch.
advisory.suggested_fix: Capture the starting tip and call `update-ref branch merged_sha <old_tip>` (empty string when unborn) so a concurrent mover aborts the publish.

evidence: src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:321-322: off-ref path uses `update-ref` and 'leaving the worktree untouched'
src/rebar/_store/push.py:539-544: on multi-bundle it heals then `continue`s the loop, re-running the same `HEAD:{branch}` push
test test_heal_folds_into_the_ref_from_a_side_branch_tracker asserts HEAD stays at `side` while refs/heads/tickets == merged (test_s3_doctor.py:240-242)
advisory.finding: After an off-ref heal (side-branch or detached HEAD), the doctor leaves the worktree HEAD unmoved but publishes the merged tip only into refs/heads/<ref>. The sole caller in push.py retries the push with `git push remote HEAD:{branch}` (HEAD, not refs/heads/<ref>), so the retried push publishes the tracker's checked-out branch tip rather than the newly-folded ref tip.

evidence: src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:277-281: `if merged.returncode != 0:` raises S3DoctorConflict for ALL non-zero returns
src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:356-369: the bundle step distinguishes transient object-read faults from conflicts and adjusts the hint
S3DoctorConflict default hint (s3_doctor.py:43) sends the operator to `rebar fsck-recover`
advisory.finding: _fold_heads treats any non-zero return from `merge-tree --write-tree` as an S3DoctorConflict carrying the default fsck-recover hint, conflating a genuine content conflict (exit 1) with a hard git error (exit 128, e.g. a bad/unreadable object). _publish_and_prune deliberately distinguishes these for the bundle step (is_transient_object_read_error) to avoid sending operators to the wrong tool; the fold step does not.
